hints: A palindrome reads identically in both directions.
Treat each position and each gap as a possible center.
Manacher's algorithm reuses mirrored palindrome radii to avoid repeated scans.
analogy: A palindrome is a mirror: a known wide mirror tells you how far smaller mirrors inside it already match.
example: In babad, bab and aba both have length 3, so either is a longest answer.
algorithm: Compute the longest odd and even palindrome radius at every center using Manacher's algorithm. Maintain the rightmost known palindrome and use the mirrored center to initialize a radius before extending it. Return the substring with greatest length.
correctness: Every radius starts from characters known to match by symmetry and is then extended until a mismatch or boundary, so it is maximal. Every palindrome has an odd or even center, hence the largest radius gives a longest one.
complexity: For string length n, O(n) time and O(n) space.
